evals.name: routing-triggers
evals.prompt: work through docs/billing/todo.md and build all the remaining phases
evals.expected_output: plan-run loads, reads docs/billing/todo.md, takes every unticked ### Phase N block in numeric order, shows the run list with each phase's tier and Done when: for approval, then builds them one at a time through the implement and review Workflows — merging each and ticking its boxes, and halting the whole run at the first phase that fails.

evals.name: routing-excludes-task-run
evals.expected_output: One named phase handed over directly is task-run's job; plan-run must not load, because there is no sequence of phases to carry through in order and nothing for the halt-on-failure rule to protect.

evals.name: routing-excludes-issues-fix
evals.prompt: work through the list in issues.md and fix everything in it
evals.expected_output: A flat backlog of independent items is issues-fix's job — it verifies each against the code, groups items one change can fix together, and a failed group never stops the loop. plan-run must not load: there are no ### Phase headings, no dependency order to respect, and grouping is exactly what plan-run refuses to do.

evals.name: routing-excludes-spec-design
evals.prompt: take docs/billing/spec.html and break it into phases with a done-when check for each
evals.expected_output: Writing the plan is spec-design's job; plan-run must not load, because there is no todo.md to execute yet — it consumes the phases spec-design produces.

evals.name: routing-triggers-resume
evals.prompt: carry on with the implementation plan from phase 4, I fixed what phase 3 got wrong
evals.expected_output: plan-run loads and resolves this to --from 4: it starts at Phase 4 whatever the earlier checkboxes say, never re-runs phases 1-3, and runs the rest in numeric order. This is the resume path a halted run reports.

evals.name: phase-failure-halts-rather-than-building-on-top
evals.expected_output: The first phase that fails — implement stopped, review blocked, build red, or its own Done when: check failing — halts the run. Later phases are not attempted on top of it, the branch is left in place unmerged, and the report names the halt reason and the resume command.

evals.name: no-merge-refuses-from-the-primary-tree
evals.expected_output: Run from the primary working tree, --no-merge stops and prints the git worktree add --detach command instead of running. A --no-merge run there would strand the user's own checkout on a phase branch with a finished commit and no merge. The slice is also checked against the graph first, and a missing checker is a halt, not a named skip.

evals.name: phases-run-in-the-plan-order-never-regrouped
evals.expected_output: Every unticked phase runs in its written order, one at a time. Phases are never reordered, folded together or re-derived — the plan already carries each phase's Files:, Risk: and runnable Done when:, and each is re-checked against the current code just before it runs. --cmux does not change this: it batches by a wave the plan itself declares through its Depends on: edges, and lands each wave in ascending phase order, so no phase is reordered against another it depends on and no two phases are ever folded into one run.

evals.name: cmux-drives-the-existing-protocol-and-never-invents-parallelism
evals.expected_output: Only leaves the plan's own dependency graph puts in the same wave are built at once, and only after check_todo.py --slice clears them. Every leaf gets a full interactive claude session in its own detached worktree and cmux workspace, a wave of one included — the wave decides how many run at once, never whether a workspace is opened, and nothing is built inline in the orchestrator's tree. A solo leaf is landed before the next worktree is cut, since a detached worktree is pinned to the base it was created from. At most steps.fanout.maxUnits are live at a time (default 3), and each one's workspace and worktree are taken down the moment it comes back ok — freeing the slot for the next leaf. A unit that failed or stalled is left standing and named. The wave is landed from the primary tree in ascending phase order. Without --cmux none of this happens: the run is the serial one, phase by phase.

evals.name: messages-raise-alarms-but-never-close-a-unit
evals.expected_output: Units are spawned with --orchestrator so they can message up to the orchestrator, and they send only in four cases: they are about to write a file their Files: line does not name, they are blocked on something the plan can answer, a test they did not write is failing, or they are halting. A unit reporting an undeclared file is recorded against its phase and told to continue — Files: is written before the code exists — and only a second unit claiming the same file halts the wave. Nothing lands on a message: wait still blocks on the sentinel and landing still requires the branch marker, because a session can go idle having declined its work. The orchestrator may answer questions and ask read-only checks, but never drives a unit and never polls it in place of wait. The concurrency cap comes from steps.fanout.maxUnits in the config (default 3), resolved by the fan-out script.
